analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 456-467). It describes NAX-GPU (M5+) kernel routing for Nemotron Super NVFP4 experts (ModelOptNVFP4NAXExperts) and dense projections (ModelOptNAXDenseLinear). It also describes the speculative-round verify-window submit cadence (DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP_WINDOW_SUBMIT) and the fused decode kernel switch (DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP_FUSION=0 to restore op chains). No executable source, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache-scope, or coordinator wire contract appears in the diff. The doc claims that the new kernels and env knobs change no token, and that expert summation order differs while teacher-forced accuracy does not. These numerical-equivalence claims are not backed by code in this batch, and the underlying kernel changes are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify them. This bears on T-007 and T-027 (output integrity, which is unattested in any case) and on the exactness assumptions of prefix-cache reuse in T-041. The note that the expert summation order differs from grouped GEMM could matter if checkpoint restores are expected to be bit-identical across kernel paths. The doc says checkpoints sit at chunk multiples so restores continue a cold prefill bit for bit, but that claim is not demonstrated for NAX kernels. This is a numerical-consistency question, not a demonstrated security regression. The new env vars are local operator knobs on the provider process, which sits inside the operator's own trust domain (TB-003), and they add no remote attack surface. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the NAX kernel and fusion code, if shipped in other PR files, preserves cache-scope partitioning, the memory-budget charges (the unmeasured scratch allowance), and the fail-closed behavior for non-finite results. These are outside this batch. No findings.
